relevance_note: Case report of one girl with a TNFAIP3 deletion: 'validated that the patient had a de novo 119 kb microdeletion involving only TNFAIP3', plus four previously published deletion carriers in Table 1.
method_note: Read the whole paper including the converted Supplementary Table S1; built the JSON with a short Python script in scratch that copies table cells by parsing the Markdown lines, and every span was checked verbatim by script. Table 1 shows patients as columns (column header row label 'Location'; data column 1 = 'This report' = the case-report patient, labelled 'patient'; columns 2-5 = previously published patients, labelled 'Table 1 column k', with the References cell copied to source_reference_in_review). Column spans quote the row from its row label through that column. Table 1 'Range of deletion' row label states the build (GRCh37/hg19). In scope: the patient, her mother (II-2) and father (II-1), who were tested. Grandparents: DNA was extracted and their c.305A>G genotypes are only in the Fig. 1D pedigree, with no number or individual detail in text, so no rows. Left out of variants: TNFAIP3 c.305A > G (NM_001270507.2), which the authors describe as relatively common (MAF = 0.0117) and use only as a marker (patient apparently homozygous A/A, mother heterozygous A/G, father G/G); it is treated as a common non-causal variant. Contradictions/inconsistencies: WES-based EXCAVATOR2 reports a 187 kb microdeletion 'within the TNFAIP3 gene' while the SNP array gives 119 kb 'involving only TNFAIP3'; one variant row recorded with the SNP-array description. De novo recorded because the paper states CNV analysis of the patient and both parents (Supplementary Fig. S1 legend) and calls the deletion de novo; only the father is explicitly stated to lack the deletion on the SNP array. Zygosity 'heterozygous' is from 'The present case suggests that HA20 caused by TNFAIP3 heterozygous microdeletion'. Laboratory values with printed normal ranges (CRP, ESR, IL-6, sTNFR-1, sTNFR-2, IL-18, IL-10, ANA speckled 80x) recorded as elevated/low/positive; normal or negative tests recorded as excluded abnormality per D-27. 'Esophagogastroduodenoscopy findings were unremarkable', 'The terminal ileum was normal' and the immunological workup with 'no apparent abnormalities' are whole investigations and are recorded as written, excluding nothing more specific. Not used: 'Although she was afebrile' (state at 8 months, not an exclusion of recurrent fever); screening tests at 1 month 'not consistent with primary immunodeficiency, autoinflammatory disease, or hemophagocytic syndrome' (diagnostic screening, not a feature); 'no ... other significant family medical history' (not specific features for the parents). Perianal ulcers/fistulae were not counted as gastrointestinal or genital ulcers in the checklist; 'thyroiditis' (Table 1 column 4) was not counted as autoimmune thyroiditis because 'autoimmune' is not stated; 'psychomotor delay' and 'headache' not counted as CNS involvement. Age at last evaluation left not reported: the patient is introduced as 8 months old but follow-up continued 'for 1 year after' seton placement, with no age given. No stacked ' / ' cells.
